MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence about factors and multiples is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6; multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on
   B. A number has more factors than multiples
   C. Factors of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on; multiples are 1, 2, 3 and 6
   D. Factors and multiples are the same thing

2. Change 28 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 4 weeks 1 days
   B. 0 weeks 4 days
   C. 5 weeks
   D. 4 weeks

3. In a tally chart, 2 groups of five and 2 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 17
   B. 13
   C. 11
   D. 12

4. Which of these is a factor of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 4
   C. 7
   D. 5

5. What is 10 L − 4 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 5 1/2 L
   B. 6 1/4 L
   C. 5 3/4 L
   D. 6 L

6. Write 5 7/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 5.07
   B. 5.7
   C. 5.007
   D. 57.0

7. In a tally chart, one group of five and 3 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 13
   C. 7
   D. 9

8. Which pattern has the rule multiply by 2? (1 mark)
   A. 5, 10, 15, 20
   B. 2, 4, 8, 16
   C. 3, 5, 7, 9
   D. 2, 4, 6, 8

9. Which decimal is equal to 0.7? (1 mark)
   A. 0.07
   B. 0.71
   C. 0.70
   D. 7.0

10. A bucket holds 10 L. A boy pours 3 cans of 2 L into it. How many more litres are needed to fill it? (1 mark)
   A. 1 L
   B. 7 L
   C. 4 L
   D. 6 L

11. One unit costs Ksh 250. What is the cost of 4 bottles of cooking oil? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,000
   B. Ksh 750
   C. Ksh 254
   D. Ksh 1,010

12. The family eats supper at half past seven at night. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 7:03 p.m.
   B. 7:30 a.m.
   C. 7:30 p.m.
   D. 7:30 noon

13. What is 18 × 50? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 68
   C. 90
   D. 9,000

14. If ? × 9 = 63, then ? is found by (1 mark)
   A. 63 ÷ 9
   B. 9 ÷ 63
   C. 63 × 9
   D. 63 − 9

15. Work out 5,127 + 2,864. (1 mark)
   A. 7,991
   B. 7,981
   C. 7,891
   D. 8,001

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In the number 27,150, give the place value and the total value of the digit 7. (4 marks)

17. Explain why the digit carried from the tens column must be added in the hundreds column when adding 3,568 + 2,276. (3 marks)

18. Box P is 5 blocks long, 2 wide and 4 high. Box Q is 4 blocks long, 4 wide and 2 high. Which has the greater volume and by how many blocks? (4 marks)

19. Name two things at home or school that are turned clockwise to tighten or close them. (2 marks)

20. Write 7,206 in expanded form. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6; multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on
   Factors divide a number exactly and are few. Multiples are found by multiplying and go on and on.

2. D — 4 weeks
   28 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 0, so 28 days = 4 weeks.

3. D — 12
   2 × 5 + 2 = 12.

4. A — 6
   18 ÷ 6 = 3 with nothing left over, so 6 is a factor of 18. The others leave a remainder.

5. C — 5 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 10 L − 4 1/4 L = 5 3/4 L.

6. A — 5.07
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 5 7/100 = 5.07.

7. A — 8
   1 × 5 + 3 = 8.

8. B — 2, 4, 8, 16
   2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. The other patterns add 2 or add 5.

9. C — 0.70
   Adding a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value. 0.7 = 0.70.

10. C — 4 L
   3 × 2 = 6 L poured in. 10 − 6 = 4 L more.

11. A — Ksh 1,000
   Cost = number × price = 4 × 250 = Ksh 1,000.

12. C — 7:30 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 7:30 p.m..

13. A — 900
   18 × 5 = 90, then × 10 gives 900.

14. A — 63 ÷ 9
   To find the missing factor we divide the product by the known factor: 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

15. A — 7,991
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 5,127 + 2,864 = 7,991.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: Place value: thousands. Total value: 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for thousands; 1 mark for 7 × 1,000; 1 mark for the answer 7,000; 1 mark for clear working.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ten tens make one hundred, so the extra 1 hundred must be counted with the hundreds. If it is left out the answer will be 100 too small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying ten tens make a hundred, 1 mark for the carried digit being added in the next column, 1 mark for the effect of leaving it out.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Box P, by 8 blocks
   Working / marking points: P = 40 (1 mark); Q = 32 (1 mark); P is greater (1 mark); 40 − 32 = 8 (1 mark).

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two, for example a bottle top or a screw, and a tap being closed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: 7,000 + 200 + 6
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7,000 and 200; 1 mark for 6 ones with no tens.
